caption:
President Trump defended Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Sunday, calling him "an honorable guy" who "probably has an excuse."
Huang admitted an affair with a woman US officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence.
Nvidia's board is investigating, and Huang stays on as CEO.

paragraphs.text: President Donald Trump defended Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang on Sunday, November 8, 2026, as the chipmaker's board opened an inquiry into Huang's relationship with a woman US intelligence officials believe worked for China. Speaking to reporters, Trump called Huang an honorable guy and said he probably had an excuse that people would need to hear, according to Anadolu Agency and The Week.

Trump said he had not spoken to Huang about the matter and described him as a fine person, while adding that one never knows what is going on, according to Euronews and The Week. He also praised the work Huang has done, saying the Nvidia chief had done an amazing job for the country, Anadolu reported.

The remarks came a day after Huang told Nvidia employees in a memo that he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologized to his family and colleagues, Newsweek reported. US officials have reportedly concluded that the woman involved was working for China's Ministry of State Security.

The New York Times has identified her as Alice Huang, a senior executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore based data center company that is under federal investigation over alleged chip smuggling into mainland China, according to Anadolu. She is not related to the Nvidia chief. The allegations about her have not been tested in court.

The New York Times also reported on November 8 that Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw a classified intelligence memo, drafted in the spring, that warned senior officials about Huang's close relationship with the suspected operative, Anadolu said. The memo circulated among national security officials before Trump's state visit to China in May. According to the same reporting, intelligence officials had been trying to identify an American whose intercepted communications pointed to an intimate relationship with Alice Huang, and a review identified Jensen Huang.

Trump reportedly declined to place restrictions on Huang or Nvidia, viewing the company's position in the chip market as important to US economic competitiveness and financial markets, Anadolu reported. The Week said Trump was asked why he had not acted despite intelligence briefings and responded that people deserve the benefit of the doubt.

Nvidia's board said it is running an independent investigation overseen by a special committee of independent directors with outside legal counsel. In its statement, the board said it prioritizes US national and economic security and has no reason to believe that national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, according to Newsweek and The Week. A company spokesperson said Huang is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption.

The president's comments give Huang political cover at a moment when the board, lawmakers and investors are all weighing the same question: whether a personal relationship created a security risk at the world's most important AI chip supplier. Trump's framing treats the matter as a personal failing until shown otherwise, while the board's review is meant to establish what, if anything, was shared.
The next marker is the outcome of the board's independent review, which will show whether Nvidia's directors find any sign that company information reached the suspected operative.
